From bb73d5d9164c57c4bb916739a98e5cd8e0a5ed8c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Claudiu Beznea <claudiu.beznea@microchip.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Aug 2022 13:28:37 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] iio: adc: at91-sama5d2_adc: fix AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX

All ADC HW versions handled by this driver (SAMA5D2, SAM9X60, SAMA7G5)
have MR.TRACKTIM on 4 bits. Fix AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX to reflect
this.

Fixes: 27e177190891 ("iio:adc:at91_adc8xx: introduce new atmel adc driver")
Signed-off-by: Claudiu Beznea <claudiu.beznea@microchip.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220803102855.2191070-2-claudiu.beznea@microchip.com
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Cameron <Jonathan.Cameron@huawei.com>

diff --git a/drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c b/drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c
index 279430c1d88c..ac9ef89fba17 100644
--- a/drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c
+++ b/drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c
@@ -77,7 +77,7 @@ struct at91_adc_reg_layout {
 #define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_ANACH		BIT(23)
 /* Tracking Time */
 #define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM(v)	((v) << 24)
-#define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX	0xff
+#define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX	0xf
 /* Transfer Time */
 #define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRANSFER(v)	((v) << 28)
 #define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRANSFER_MAX	0x3
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/iio/adc/at91-sama5d2_adc.c`**
   - The definition of `AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX` was changed from `0xff` to `0xf`. This change reflects that the `MR.TRACKTIM` field in the ADC hardware versions (SAMA5D2, SAM9X60, SAMA7G5) is only 4 bits wide, thus the maximum value should be `0xf` (15 in decimal) instead of `0xff` (255 in decimal).

### Relationships

- The modification in `at91-sama5d2_adc.c` directly addresses a bug related to the maximum value of the `MR.TRACKTIM` field in the ADC hardware versions. The previous definition incorrectly allowed for a maximum value that exceeded the actual hardware capability. This fix ensures that the driver accurately reflects the hardware specifications, thereby preventing potential issues in ADC configuration and operation. The change is linked to a previous commit that introduced the driver, indicating that this is a correction of an oversight in the initial implementation.

Here is the commit message:
iio: adc: at91-sama5d2_adc: fix AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX

All ADC HW versions handled by this driver (SAMA5D2, SAM9X60, SAMA7G5)
have MR.TRACKTIM on 4 bits. Fix AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX to reflect
this.

Fixes: 27e177190891 ("iio:adc:at91_adc8xx: introduce new atmel adc driver")
Signed-off-by: Claudiu Beznea <claudiu.beznea@microchip.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220803102855.2191070-2-claudiu.beznea@microchip.com
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Cameron <Jonathan.Cameron@huawei.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect definition of the maximum value for the `MR.TRACKTIM` field in the ADC driver, which was set to `0xff` instead of the correct `0xf`. This discrepancy arose from a misunderstanding of the hardware specifications, as all ADC hardware versions supported by the driver only utilize 4 bits for the `MR.TRACKTIM` field, leading to potential misconfigurations and erroneous behavior in ADC operations.

-#define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX	0xff
+#define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX	0xf
 /* Transfer Time */
 #define	AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRANSFER(v)	((v) << 28)

```c

```
Reason:
The maximum value for the `MR.TRACKTIM` field was incorrectly defined as `0xff`, which implies an 8-bit value, while the hardware only supports a 4-bit value. This misconfiguration can lead to erroneous behavior in ADC operations, as values exceeding `0xf` would be invalid and could cause unexpected results.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define AT91_SAMA5D2_MR_TRACKTIM_MAX 0xf
```
Reason:
The patch corrects the maximum value for the `MR.TRACKTIM` field to `0xf`, aligning it with the actual 4-bit hardware specification. This ensures that the driver correctly handles the `MR.TRACKTIM` field, preventing misconfigurations and ensuring proper ADC functionality.
